title.narrative: Lifesaving protection support for Women, Men, Boys and Girls in Drought-Affected Communities: A CERF-Funded Initiative to Combat Sexual and Gender-Based Violence

description.narrative: This project will offer immediate lifesaving support and enhancing long-term resilience and empowerment of women and girls, thereby strengthening and boosting their capacity to adapt and sustain livelihood, health, and well-being amidst severe drought that is affecting the country. Over the next six months, UNFPA will utilise the funds to deliver urgent, lifesaving sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) protection services. Specifically, the allocation will support primary GBV protection units to provide essential survivor services and fund mobile clinics across the affected regions to reach women in need of protection. Additionally, cash assistance will be offered to vulnerable community members to help them access lifesaving protection services and psychosocial support. Long-term impact will be achieved through community-level safety and security measures, including supporting existing shelters and provision of dignity kits, ensuring survivors can confidentially access necessary services and support.Project Objective: To deliver lifesaving Gender-Based Violence (GBV) protection and psychosocial support to over 19,827 individuals affected by severe drought in the Omaheke, Kavango East and Kavango West regions in Namibia.Activities include:• Provide gender-sensitive life skills information to vulnerable groups, including those in farm communities.• Enhance support for shelters and gender-based violence (GBV) protection units.• Deliver mental health and psychosocial support services.• Update and disseminate referral pathways for GBV and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA).• Provide cash voucher assistance to GBV survivors and those at risk to be able to access lifesaving services. • Implement mobile and outreach-integrated sexual and reproductive health (SRH) and GBV services in drought-affected regions.• Procure and distribute dignity kits to women and girls impacted by the drought crisis
